```{r}
#| include: false
# Creates pupils.csv; identical to simulate_pupils.R (not shown in the workshop)
set.seed(2026)   # fixes the random numbers: same data every time
n <- 120         # number of pupils

group     <- rep(c("control", "intervention"), each = n / 2)
age       <- sample(8:12, size = n, replace = TRUE)
behaviour <- rpois(n, lambda = 12)
wellbeing <- round(30 + 4 * (group == "intervention") -
                   0.5 * behaviour + rnorm(n, sd = 5))

# some pupils with many behaviour problems skip the questionnaire
no_response <- behaviour > 14 & runif(n) < 0.6
wellbeing[no_response] <- NA

pupils <- data.frame(group, age, behaviour, wellbeing)
write.csv(pupils, "pupils.csv", row.names = FALSE)
rm(list = ls())
getwd()
```

# Introduction to R and RStudio {background-color="#1a2744"}

## R and RStudio

- **R**: programming language and software environment for statistical computing and graphics
- Free and open source; extended with **packages** (e.g., from CRAN)
- **RStudio**: integrated development environment (**IDE**) for R, developed by Posit
- RStudio does not compute; it passes your commands to R
- Today: base R only, no packages needed

## Scripts, not the console

- **R script**: plain-text file (`.R`) with commands, run from top to bottom
- Run line or selection: *Ctrl* + *Enter* (Mac: *Cmd* + *Enter*)
- Run whole script: *Ctrl* + *Shift* + *Enter*
- **Comment**: text after `#` is not executed
- Objects live in memory and are lost on closing $\rightarrow$ the script is the permanent record

\vspace{0.4em}

  text width=0.95\textwidth,
  align=left
] {
\textbf{Reproducibility}: same script + same data = same output.
};
\end{tikzpicture}

## Working directory

- **Working directory**: folder where R reads and writes files by default
- Set: *Session* > *Set Working Directory* > *Choose Directory*
- Check: `getwd()`
- File names such as `"pupils.csv"` are read relative to this folder

## Core syntax

\scriptsize

| Element | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Assignment | `x <- c(3, 7, 9)` | Store values in an **object** |
| Function call | `mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)` | **Function** applied to **arguments** |
| Vector | `c(3, 7, 9)` | Ordered values of one type |
| Data frame | `pupils$age` | Rows = cases, columns = variables; `$` selects a column |
| Missing value | `NA` | "Not available" |
| Comment | `# note` | Ignored by R |

\normalsize

$\rightarrow$ Help on any function: `?mean`

## The example study

Evaluation of a classroom programme for social-emotional learning in primary school; 120 pupils, 60 per group.

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `group` | Categorical | Control or intervention |
| `age` | Whole number | Age in years (8 to 12) |
| `behaviour` | Whole number | Teacher-rated behaviour problems (higher = more problems) |
| `wellbeing` | Whole number | Self-reported wellbeing (higher = better); some missing |


## Workshop roadmap

\scriptsize

| Step | Task | Main functions |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Load the data | `read.csv()` |
| 2 | View the data | `View()`, `head()`, `str()` |
| 3 | Plot the data | `hist()`, `plot()` |
| 4 | Descriptive statistics | `summary()`, `mean()`, `sd()` |
| 5 | Group comparison plot | `tapply()`, `boxplot()` |
| 6 | t-test | `t.test()` |
| 7 | Inspect missing values | `is.na()`, `colSums()`, `table()` |
| 8 | Plot missingness on covariates | `boxplot()` |

\normalsize

$\rightarrow$ Save `pupils.csv` and `workshop.R` in one folder, set it as working directory, open `workshop.R` and work through the steps.

# Hands-on: the workshop script {background-color="#1a2744"}

## Step 1: Load the data

\scriptsize

```{r}
# stringsAsFactors = TRUE: text columns become categorical variables (factors)
pupils <- read.csv("pupils.csv", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
dim(pupils)   # number of rows and columns
```

\normalsize

$\rightarrow$ `pupils.csv` must be in the working directory; the Environment now holds `pupils`.

## Step 2: View the data

\scriptsize

```{r}
#| eval: false
View(pupils)   # spreadsheet view in a new tab
```

```{r}
head(pupils)   # first six rows
str(pupils)    # structure: type of each variable
```

\normalsize

$\rightarrow$ `Factor` = categorical, `int` = whole number, `NA` = missing value.

## Step 3: Plot the data

\scriptsize

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
hist(pupils$wellbeing, col = "steelblue",
     main = "Wellbeing", xlab = "wellbeing score")
plot(wellbeing ~ behaviour, data = pupils, pch = 19, col = "steelblue",
     main = "Wellbeing by behaviour problems")
```

\normalsize

$\rightarrow$ More behaviour problems, lower wellbeing.

## Step 4: Descriptive statistics

\scriptsize

```{r}
summary(pupils)
mean(pupils$wellbeing)                 # NA: one missing value is enough
mean(pupils$wellbeing, na.rm = TRUE)   # na.rm = TRUE: ignore missing values
sd(pupils$wellbeing, na.rm = TRUE)
```

\normalsize

$\rightarrow$ `summary()` reports `NA's`; most functions need `na.rm = TRUE`.

## Step 5: Group comparison plot

\scriptsize

```{r}
#| out-width: "45%"
tapply(pupils$wellbeing, pupils$group, mean, na.rm = TRUE)   # group means
boxplot(wellbeing ~ group, data = pupils, col = c("steelblue", "darkorange"),
        main = "Wellbeing by group", ylab = "wellbeing score")
```

\normalsize

$\rightarrow$ Intervention group higher on average; similar spread.

## Step 6: t-test

\tiny

```{r}
t.test(wellbeing ~ group, data = pupils)   # Welch two-sample t-test (default)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
tt <- t.test(wellbeing ~ group, data = pupils)
```

\normalsize

- Intervention `r round(diff(tt$estimate), 1)` points higher (95% CI `r round(-tt$conf.int[2], 1)` to `r round(-tt$conf.int[1], 1)`), $p$ < .001; true effect: +4
- Only complete cases used: $n$ = `r sum(!is.na(pupils$wellbeing))` of `r nrow(pupils)`

## Step 7: Inspect missing values

\scriptsize

```{r}
colSums(is.na(pupils))                        # number of NAs per variable
mean(is.na(pupils$wellbeing))                 # share of NAs in wellbeing
table(pupils$group, is.na(pupils$wellbeing))  # TRUE = missing
```

\normalsize

$\rightarrow$ `r sum(is.na(pupils$wellbeing))` of `r nrow(pupils)` `wellbeing` scores missing (`r round(100 * mean(is.na(pupils$wellbeing)), 1)`%); similar in both groups.

## Step 8: Plot missingness on covariates

\scriptsize

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-height: 2.8
boxplot(behaviour ~ is.na(wellbeing), data = pupils, col = "steelblue",
        names = c("observed", "missing"), xlab = "wellbeing score",
        main = "Behaviour problems")
boxplot(age ~ is.na(wellbeing), data = pupils, col = "steelblue",
        names = c("observed", "missing"), xlab = "wellbeing score",
        main = "Age")
```

\normalsize

$\rightarrow$ Missingness related to `behaviour`, not to `age`: not missing completely at random.
